samasa.vigraha: कार्यम् च कारणम् च कार्यकारणे; कार्यकारणाभ्याम् निर्मुक्ता कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāryam ca kāraṇam ca kāryakāraṇe; kāryakāraṇābhyām nirmuktā kāryakāraṇanirmuktā
samasa.explanation: (1) kārya-kāraṇa 'effect and cause' (dvandva). (2) The participle nirmuktā 'released, free' is the head and takes the pair in the ablative: 'free from effect and cause'.

components.note: the prefix nir 'out, without' (listed among the prefixes also as nis) + √muc 'to release', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is free from the bond of cause and effect
names.significance: Traditionally She is the Absolute, which is neither an effect of anything nor, in its own nature, a cause; causality belongs to the world She projects, not to Her.
names.previous_split_issues: kārya was glossed 'purpose/work'; paired with kāraṇa 'cause' it means 'effect'.

samasa.vigraha: कामस्य केलिः कामकेलिः; कामकेलिभिः तरङ्गिता कामकेलितरङ्गिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmasya keliḥ kāmakeliḥ; kāmakelibhiḥ taraṅgitā kāmakelitaraṅgitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-keli 'the love-play of Kāma (Kāmeśvara)' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) taraṅgitā 'made to surge in waves' is the head, with that play as its instrument.

names.meaning: She who surges in waves of joy in Her love-play with Kāmeśvara
names.significance: Traditionally the play of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī is the bliss of Śiva and Śakti in union, and the waves of that bliss are the worlds that arise from it.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'kAmeshvara' respelled; taraṅgitā 'surging in waves' made explicit.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कनकस्य ताटङ्कौ कनकताटङ्कौ; कनन्तौ कनकताटङ्कौ कनत्कनकताटङ्कौ; कनत्कनकताटङ्कौ यस्याः सा कनत्कनकताटङ्का
samasa.vigraha_iast: kanakasya tāṭaṅkau kanakatāṭaṅkau; kanantau kanakatāṭaṅkau kanatkanakatāṭaṅkau; kanatkanakatāṭaṅkau yasyāḥ sā kanatkanakatāṭaṅkā
samasa.explanation: (1) kanaka-tāṭaṅka 'earrings of gold' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa of material). (2) The present participle kanat 'shining' qualifies them (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose earrings are of shining gold'; tāṭaṅka takes the feminine -ā. The t of kanat is unchanged before k.

components.note: tāṭaṅka with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who wears glittering gold ear ornaments
names.significance: Her earrings are a sign of Her auspicious wifehood: the Saundaryalaharī (verse 28) ascribes Śiva's survival of the poison He swallowed to the power of Her tāṭaṅkas.

samasa.vigraha: लीलया विग्रहाः लीलाविग्रहाः; लीलाविग्रहान् धारयति इति लीलाविग्रहधारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: līlayā vigrahāḥ līlāvigrahāḥ; līlāvigrahān dhārayati iti līlāvigrahadhāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) līlā-vigraha 'forms taken in play' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) dhāriṇī 'bearing, assuming' (causative of √dhṛ + -in) is the head, with the forms as its object.

names.meaning: She who takes on forms in play
names.significance: She has no need to take a body; Her incarnations and manifestations are play (līlā), undertaken freely for the good of the worlds.

meaning_check.note: 'various glorious' is not in the name.

samasa.vigraha: न जायते इति अजा
samasa.vigraha_iast: na jāyate iti ajā
samasa.explanation: The negative a- is joined to ja 'born' (from √jan, which occurs only at the end of a compound): 'not born'; feminine -ā.

components.note: the negative particle na in composition

names.meaning: She who has no birth
names.significance: The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad speaks of the one unborn (ajā), red, white and black, who brings forth many offspring like herself: Prakṛti with its three guṇas. Ajā also means 'she-goat', the image that verse plays on.

samasa.vigraha: क्षयात् विनिर्मुक्ता क्षयविनिर्मुक्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣayāt vinirmuktā kṣayavinirmuktā
samasa.explanation: The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly released' is the head and kṣaya 'decay' stands to it in the ablative.

components.note: vi + the prefix nir 'out, without' (listed among the prefixes also as nis) + √muc, past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who is free from decay
names.significance: Being unborn (866) She does not decay; time, which wastes all things, has no hold on Her.

names.meaning: She who is captivating in Her beauty
names.significance: The participle also means 'innocent, artless': Her beauty is that of simplicity, and it bewilders even Śiva.

samasa.vigraha: क्षिप्रम् प्रसीदति इति क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kṣipram prasīdati iti kṣipraprasādinī
samasa.explanation: prasādinī is an agent noun in -in of habit (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye) from pra + √sad 'to become clear, gracious'; the adverb kṣipra 'quickly' is the upapada: 'one who is quickly gracious'.

names.meaning: She who is quickly pleased
names.significance: Traditionally She is easily and swiftly moved to grace, even by a little devotion.

samasa.vigraha: अन्तः मुखम् येषाम् ते अन्तर्मुखाः; अन्तर्मुखैः समाराध्या अन्तर्मुखसमाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: antaḥ mukham yeṣām te antarmukhāḥ; antarmukhaiḥ samārādhyā antarmukhasamārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) antar-mukha 'those whose face is turned within' (bahuvrīhi). (2) The gerundive samārādhyā 'to be worshipped fully' is the head, with those people as its agents in the instrumental. The r of antar is original.

components.note: sam + ā + √rādh 'to propitiate' + the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is to be worshipped by those whose gaze is turned within
names.significance: Traditionally inward worship (antar-yāga), with the mind withdrawn from the senses, is the highest form of Her worship.

meaning_check.note: The compound names the worshippers (those turned within); 'internally (mentally)' paraphrased that.

names.previous_split_issues: samārādhyā is a gerundive, 'to be worshipped', not 'worshipped by'.

sandhi.rule: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which stands as r before a voiced consonant

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and a prādi compound)
samasa.vigraha: बहिः मुखम् येषाम् ते बहिर्मुखाः; दुःखेन लभ्यते इति दुर्लभा; सुतराम् दुर्लभा सुदुर्लभा; बहिर्मुखैः सुदुर्लभा बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: bahiḥ mukham yeṣām te bahirmukhāḥ; duḥkhena labhyate iti durlabhā; sutarām durlabhā sudurlabhā; bahirmukhaiḥ sudurlabhā bahirmukhasudurlabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) bahir-mukha 'those whose face is turned outward' (bahuvrīhi). (2) dur-labha 'hard to obtain' (the suffix -a after dur, Pāṇini 3.3.126), intensified by su 'very' (prādi). (3) The whole: 'very hard to obtain for those turned outward' (instrumental of agent). The counterpart of name 870.

components.meaning: with difficulty (prefix; listed also as dus)

names.meaning: She who is difficult to attain by those whose attention is directed outwards
names.significance: Those whose minds run outward through the senses do not find Her, though She is nearest of all; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says the Self-born pierced the senses outward, and only the one who turns the gaze within sees the Self.
names.previous_split_issues: bahir was given in its sandhi form (the word is bahis); su was glossed 'good/beautiful' — here it intensifies, 'very'.

names.meaning: She who is the three Vedas
names.significance: Trayī is the old name for the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas together; the name also covers every triad — the three guṇas, three states, three worlds — that She comprises.

meaning_check.note: Capitalized Vedas.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally (over an inner dvigu)
samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् वर्गः त्रिवर्गः; त्रिवर्गस्य निलयः त्रिवर्गनिलयः; त्रिवर्गनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति त्रिवर्गनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām vargaḥ trivargaḥ; trivargasya nilayaḥ trivarganilayaḥ; trivarganilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti trivarganilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-varga 'the group of three', i.e. dharma, artha and kāma (a numeral compound, dvigu). (2) …-nilaya 'abode of that group' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

components.note: ni + √lī 'to rest in'; nilaya with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is the abode of the threefold aims of human life
names.significance: The trivarga is dharma, artha and kāma, the three aims of life in the world; She is their ground, and beyond them She grants the fourth, mokṣa.

samasa.vigraha: त्रिषु तिष्ठति इति त्रिस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: triṣu tiṣṭhati iti tristhā
samasa.explanation: stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with tri 'three' in the locative plural as the upapada: 'abiding in the three'; feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who abides in the three worlds, the three times and the three states
names.significance: The name leaves 'three' open; traditionally it covers the three worlds, the three times (past, present, future), the three states (waking, dream, sleep) and the three deities of creation, preservation and dissolution.

meaning_check.note: 'worlds' is only one of the triads the name can mean; the others are added.

samasa.type: dvigu (samāhāra), followed by a possessive in -in
samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरम् माला अस्याः अस्ति इति त्रिपुरमालिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripuram mālā asyāḥ asti iti tripuramālinī
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (a numeral compound denoting the group, dvigu). (2) mālinī 'garlanded' (mālā + the possessive -in): 'She who has the three cities as Her garland'. As the proper name of a Śrīcakra deity the name is not usually analysed further.

names.meaning: She who is Tripuramālinī, the presiding Goddess of the inner ten-triangle enclosure (antardaśāra) of the Śrīcakra
names.significance: In the Śrīcakra each enclosure has a presiding Goddess whose name begins with Tripura-; Tripuramālinī rules the sixth, the inner ten triangles.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'antardashAra' and 'shrI chakra' respelled.

names.previous_split_issues: mālinī was glossed 'possessing'; it is 'garlanded' (mālā + -in).
names.uncertain: As a proper name its internal analysis is not fixed; the vigraha given is grammatical, not a traditional gloss.

samasa.vigraha: निर्गतः आमयः यस्याः सा निरामया
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirgataḥ āmayaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirāmayā
samasa.explanation: The prefix nir stands for nirgata 'gone out': 'She from whom disease (āmaya) is gone'; āmaya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: the prefix nir 'out, without' (listed among the prefixes also as nis)
āmaya with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is free from diseases of all kinds
names.significance: Free of every affliction of body and mind, She also frees Her devotees from them.

samasa.vigraha: निर्गतः आलम्बः यस्याः सा निरालम्बा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirgataḥ ālambaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirālambā
samasa.explanation: 'She from whom support (ālamba) is gone', i.e. who rests on nothing; ālamba takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: the prefix nir 'out, without' (listed among the prefixes also as nis)
ā + √lamb 'to hang on'; ālamba with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who depends on none
names.significance: She is the support of all and is Herself supported by nothing.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a saptamī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: स्वः आत्मा स्वात्मा; स्वात्मनि आरामः स्वात्मारामः; स्वात्मारामः यस्याः सा स्वात्मारामा
samasa.vigraha_iast: svaḥ ātmā svātmā; svātmani ārāmaḥ svātmārāmaḥ; svātmārāmaḥ yasyāḥ sā svātmārāmā
samasa.explanation: (1) sva-ātman 'one's own self' (karmadhāraya; ātman appears as ātma- with loss of the final n). (2) svātma-ārāma 'delight in one's own self' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose delight is in Her own self'.

components.note: appears as ātma- in the compound
ā + √ram 'to delight'; ārāma with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who rejoices in Her own self
names.significance: She needs nothing outside Herself for joy; the Upaniṣads call such a one ātmārāma, 'delighting in the Self'.
names.previous_split_issues: The old split 'svātmā + rāmā' cut through a fused vowel: the members are sva + ātman + ārāma, and the reading form is no longer hyphenated there.

samasa.vigraha: सुधायाः सृतिः सुधासृतिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: sudhāyāḥ sṛtiḥ sudhāsṛtiḥ
samasa.explanation: sṛti 'flowing, course' is the head and nectar stands to it in the genitive: 'the stream of nectar'. The feminine noun sṛti keeps its nominative -iḥ.

names.meaning: She who is the stream of nectar
names.significance: In the kuṇḍalinī practice nectar flows from the moon in the thousand-petalled lotus once the power reaches it; She is that stream, which drenches the subtle body.

meaning_check.note: 'source' sharpened to 'stream': sṛti is a flowing.

names.previous_split_issues: The old split carried the slash alternative 'srutiḥ / sṛtiḥ'; the text reads sṛtiḥ (see variants).
names.variants: Some editions read सुधास्रुतिः sudhāsrutiḥ (√sru 'to flow'), with the same sense.

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before s (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), inside the lexicalised saṃsāra
after d, h becomes dh, the aspirate of the preceding stop (optional, Pāṇini 8.4.62 jhayo ho 'nyatarasyām)

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya of identification)
samasa.vigraha: संसारः एव पङ्कः संसारपङ्कः; संसारपङ्के निर्मग्नाः संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नाः; संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नानाम् समुद्धरणम् संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणम्; संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणे पण्डिता संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणपण्डिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: saṃsāraḥ eva paṅkaḥ saṃsārapaṅkaḥ; saṃsārapaṅke nirmagnāḥ saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnāḥ; saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnānām samuddharaṇam saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇam; saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇe paṇḍitā saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā
samasa.explanation: (1) saṃsāra-paṅka 'the mire that is saṃsāra' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) …-nirmagna 'sunk in that mire' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …-samuddharaṇa 'the lifting out of those so sunk' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) paṇḍitā 'skilled' is the head, with the rescue as the field of skill in the locative.

components.note: the prefix nir 'out, without' (listed among the prefixes also as nis) + √masj 'to sink', past participle

names.meaning: She who is skilled in raising those who are immersed in the mire of transmigratory life
names.significance: Traditionally saṃsāra is a mire in which the soul sinks deeper the more it struggles; She, standing outside it, is expert at lifting the soul out.

samasa.vigraha: यज्ञः प्रियः यस्याः सा यज्ञप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: yajñaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā yajñapriyā
samasa.explanation: 'She to whom sacrifice (yajña) is dear (priya)'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: priya with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is fond of sacrifices and other rites
names.significance: Every sacrifice, outer or inner, reaches Her; in Śrīvidyā the inner sacrifice of offering the mind into consciousness is the dearest of all.

meaning_check.note: Missing 'of' supplied.

samasa.vigraha: यज्ञस्य कर्त्री यज्ञकर्त्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: yajñasya kartrī yajñakartrī
samasa.explanation: kartrī 'doer, performer' (agent noun from √kṛ) is the head and the sacrifice stands to it in the genitive (on compounds with -tṛ see name 811).

names.meaning: She who is the doer of sacrificial rites
names.significance: Traditionally She is the real agent in every rite; the priest and the patron act by Her power.
names.previous_split_issues: kartrī was glossed 'creator'; here it is 'doer, performer' of the rite.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: यजमानः एव स्वरूपम् यजमानस्वरूपम्; यजमानस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति यजमानस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: yajamānaḥ eva svarūpam yajamānasvarūpam; yajamānasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti yajamānasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) yajamāna-svarūpa 'the nature that is the yajamāna' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) The possessive suffix -in makes it 'She whose own form is the yajamāna'.

components.meaning: the patron of a sacrifice, who has it performed for himself

components.note: svarūpa 'own form, nature' (sva + rūpa) + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who has the form of the yajamāna, the patron who offers the sacrifice
names.significance: The yajamāna is one of the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti) of Śiva, with the five elements, the sun and the moon; She bears that form as His power.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'yajamAna' respelled; the yajamāna is the patron for whom the rite is performed, not the one who directs it.

names.previous_split_issues: svarūpiṇī was left as one row with no account of sva + rūpa + -in; yajamāna is the patron, not a 'performer'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: धर्मस्य आधारः धर्माधारः; धर्माधारः अस्याः अस्ति इति धर्माधारा
samasa.vigraha_iast: dharmasya ādhāraḥ dharmādhāraḥ; dharmādhāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti dharmādhārā
samasa.explanation: (1) dharma-ādhāra 'the support of dharma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, ādhāra the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

components.meaning: dharma: right order, duty, the law that upholds

names.meaning: She who is the support of dharma
names.significance: Dharma upholds the world, and She upholds dharma: She is the ground on which right order stands, as both its source and its protector.

meaning_check.note: 'the code for righteous living' narrows dharma; the word is kept.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is dharma + ādhāra, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the lexicalised adhyakṣa 'overseer'

samasa.vigraha: धनस्य अध्यक्षा धनाध्यक्षा
samasa.vigraha_iast: dhanasya adhyakṣā dhanādhyakṣā
samasa.explanation: adhyakṣā 'overseer, presiding lady' is the head and wealth stands to it in the genitive.

components.note: adhi 'over' + akṣa 'eye': 'one with an eye over'; feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who oversees wealth
names.significance: Dhanādhyakṣa is a title of Kubera, lord of riches; traditionally She is the power behind Kubera and the giver of wealth to those who worship Her.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is dhana + adhyakṣā (adhi + akṣa), fused by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.vigraha: धनम् च धान्यम् च धनधान्ये; धनधान्ययोः विवर्धिनी धनधान्यविवर्धिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: dhanam ca dhānyam ca dhanadhānye; dhanadhānyayoḥ vivardhinī dhanadhānyavivardhinī
samasa.explanation: (1) dhana-dhānya 'wealth and grain' (dvandva). (2) vivardhinī 'one who increases' is the head, with the pair in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who increases wealth and harvests
names.significance: Traditionally She gives prosperity in money and in food to the householder who worships Her.

samasa.vigraha: विप्राः प्रियाः यस्याः सा विप्रप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: viprāḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā viprapriyā
samasa.explanation: 'She to whom the learned (vipra) are dear (priya)'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: the learned, inspired sage; a brāhmaṇa

components.note: priya with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is fond of the learned
names.significance: Traditionally the vipra is one who knows the Veda and Brahman; such knowers are dear to Her.

samasa.vigraha: विप्रः रूपम् यस्याः सा विप्ररूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: vipraḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā viprarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form (rūpa) is the vipra'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: the learned sage, knower of Brahman

components.note: rūpa with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has the form of the vipra, the knower of the Self
names.significance: Traditionally She is present in the sage who knows Brahman, and Her worship is completed by honoring such a one.

meaning_check.note: Wording tidied; vipra kept in view.

samasa.vigraha: विश्वस्य भ्रमणम् विश्वभ्रमणम्; विश्वभ्रमणम् करोति इति विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvasya bhramaṇam viśvabhramaṇam; viśvabhramaṇam karoti iti viśvabhramaṇakāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) viśva-bhramaṇa 'the revolving of the universe' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) kāriṇī 'one who causes' (√kṛ + -in) is the head, with that revolving as its object.

names.meaning: She who makes the universe go around through Her power of illusion
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā (18.61) says the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, 'causing them to revolve by māyā as if mounted on a machine'; She turns the worlds and the wandering of souls.

samasa.vigraha: विश्वम् ग्रासः यस्याः सा विश्वग्रासा; अथवा विश्वम् ग्रसते इति विश्वग्रासा
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvam grāsaḥ yasyāḥ sā viśvagrāsā; athavā viśvam grasate iti viśvagrāsā
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose morsel (grāsa) is the universe'. As an upapada-tatpuruṣa: 'She who swallows the universe' (grāsa from √gras with vṛddhi). The sense is the same.

names.meaning: She who devours the universe
names.significance: At dissolution the whole universe is a mouthful to Her; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of the one for whom priest and warrior are food and death itself the sauce.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: विद्रुमस्य इव आभा यस्याः सा विद्रुमाभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: vidrumasya iva ābhā yasyāḥ sā vidrumābhā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose radiance (ābhā) is like that of coral (vidruma)'. ābhā is already feminine.

names.meaning: She who shines like coral (with Her red complexion)
names.significance: Her complexion is red like coral, the color of compassion and of the rising sun in which She is meditated.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is vidruma + ābhā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

components.meaning: belonging to Viṣṇu; the power of Viṣṇu
components.note: viṣṇu + the suffix -a with vṛddhi of the first vowel, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the power of Viṣṇu
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya hails Her as vaiṣṇavī śaktir anantavīryā, 'the power of Viṣṇu, of boundless might, the seed of the universe'; Vaiṣṇavī is also one of the Mātṛkās.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'viShNu' respelled; the derivative means 'of Viṣṇu', His power.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: विष्णुः एव रूपम् विष्णुरूपम्; विष्णुरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विष्णुरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: viṣṇuḥ eva rūpam viṣṇurūpam; viṣṇurūpam asyāḥ asti iti viṣṇurūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) viṣṇu-rūpa 'the form that is Viṣṇu'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is Viṣṇu'.

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who has the form of Viṣṇu, the all-pervading
names.significance: The older rendering, 'a form that extends over the whole universe', gives the traditional etymology of Viṣṇu as the pervader; She is that pervading presence.

meaning_check.note: The name says 'having the form of Viṣṇu'; the old rendering gave only the etymology of Viṣṇu, now in the significance.

samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते योनिः यस्याः सा अयोनिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: na vidyate yoniḥ yasyāḥ sā ayoniḥ
samasa.explanation: 'She for whom there is no source (yoni)': the negative a- and yoni form a bahuvrīhi. The feminine i-stem keeps its nominative -iḥ.

components.note: the negative particle na in composition

names.meaning: She who is without origin
names.significance: She is the uncaused source; nothing precedes Her. The next name turns this around: She is the abode of every source.

samasa.vigraha: योनीनाम् निलयः योनिनिलयः; योनिनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति योनिनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: yonīnām nilayaḥ yoninilayaḥ; yoninilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti yoninilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) yoni-nilaya 'the abode of the sources' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X'). A locative reading, 'She who dwells in the yoni', is also current.

components.meaning: source, origin, womb; the central triangle of the Śrīcakra

names.meaning: She who is the seat of all origins
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the yoni is also the central triangle (trikoṇa) of the Śrīcakra, the womb of the worlds, in which She dwells.
names.uncertain: Read as 'the abode of all sources' or as 'She who dwells in the yoni (the central triangle)'.

samasa.vigraha: कूटे तिष्ठति इति कूटस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: kūṭe tiṣṭhati iti kūṭasthā
samasa.explanation: stha 'standing' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with kūṭa as the upapada: 'standing like (on) an anvil', i.e. immovable; feminine -ā.

components.meaning: anvil; peak; heap; a group (as the kūṭas of a mantra)

names.meaning: She who remains unchanged like the anvil
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā calls the imperishable Self kūṭastha, unchanging like the anvil on which everything is shaped. In Śrīvidyā the name is also read as She who abides in the three kūṭas (sections) of the Pañcadaśī mantra.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: कुलम् एव रूपम् कुलरूपम्; कुलरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति कुलरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kulam eva rūpam kularūpam; kularūpam asyāḥ asti iti kularūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) kula-rūpa 'the form that is kula'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is kula'.

components.meaning: family, lineage; in Tantra the Kaula path, and the triad of knower, knowing and known

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She whose form is kula, the deity of the Kaula path
names.significance: In the Kaula tradition kula is Śakti and the whole manifest world, and also the triad of knower, knowing and known; She is all of these and is worshipped as the deity of the Kaula path.

meaning_check.note: The old rendering kept as the second half; the rūpiṇī ('whose form is kula') made explicit and kaula capitalized as Kaula.

samasa.vigraha: वीराणाम् गोष्ठी वीरगोष्ठी; वीरगोष्ठी प्रिया यस्याः सा वीरगोष्ठीप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: vīrāṇām goṣṭhī vīragoṣṭhī; vīragoṣṭhī priyā yasyāḥ sā vīragoṣṭhīpriyā
samasa.explanation: (1) vīra-goṣṭhī 'the assembly of heroes' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom that assembly is dear'.

components.meaning: hero; in Tantra the adept of the heroic disposition

names.meaning: She who is fond of the assembly of warriors
names.significance: Traditionally both the gathering of warriors and the circle of Tantric adepts (vīras) who meet for Her worship.

names.meaning: She who is heroic
names.significance: Her heroism is shown in the destruction of Bhaṇḍa and the demons; She is also the mother and refuge of heroes (836).

components.note: naiṣkarmya 'freedom from action', abstract noun from niṣkarman 'without action' (nis + karman) with vṛddhi; feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is beyond all action (naiṣkarmya)
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā speaks of naiṣkarmya-siddhi, the perfection of freedom from action; though all action flows from Her power, She is untouched by it, being Her own fulfillment.

meaning_check.note: 'abstains from actions' suggests refraining; naiṣkarmya is the state beyond action.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: नादः एव रूपम् नादरूपम्; नादरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति नादरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: nādaḥ eva rūpam nādarūpam; nādarūpam asyāḥ asti iti nādarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) nāda-rūpa 'the form that is nāda'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is nāda'.

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the primal sound
names.significance: In the Tantric account of creation nāda is the first stirring of sound from the bindu, from which the letters and mantras arise; in the mantra it is the subtle resonance after the anusvāra.

samasa.vigraha: विज्ञानस्य कलना विज्ञानकलना
samasa.vigraha_iast: vijñānasya kalanā vijñānakalanā
samasa.explanation: kalanā 'grasping, realizing' is the head and vijñāna stands to it in the genitive: 'the realizing of (supreme) knowledge'.

components.meaning: discerning knowledge; realized knowledge of Brahman

names.meaning: She who is the realization of supreme knowledge (vijñāna)
names.significance: Traditionally vijñāna is the direct experience of Brahman as distinct from book-learning; She is that realization itself.

meaning_check.note: 'of brahman' is not in the name; vijñāna is realized knowledge, which She is.

names.previous_split_issues: kalanā was glossed 'creation/art'; here it is 'grasping, realizing'.

names.meaning: She who is able, sound and auspicious
names.significance: Kalya means 'ready, capable' and 'whole, healthy', and also 'auspicious, of the dawn'; She is ever ready to grant what is sought.

meaning_check.note: 'of creation' is not in the name.

names.uncertain: kalya has several senses (able, healthy, auspicious; also 'dawn'), and traditional glosses differ; the rendering combines the main ones.

components.note: vi + √dah 'to burn', past participle: lit. 'well-cooked', i.e. mature, accomplished

names.meaning: She who is expert in everything
names.significance: She is the accomplished one, skilled in every art and in the conduct of the world.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: बैन्दवम् आसनम् यस्याः सा बैन्दवासना
samasa.vigraha_iast: baindavam āsanam yasyāḥ sā baindavāsanā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose seat (āsana) is the baindava', the place of the bindu; āsana takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She whose seat is the bindu, the central point of the Śrīcakra
names.significance: The baindava-sthāna is the innermost point of the Śrīcakra, the sarvānandamaya cakra, where She sits with Kāmeśvara.

meaning_check.note: The baindava place is the central point (bindu) of the Śrīcakra, not 'the spot between the eyebrows', which is the ājñā.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is baindava + āsana, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तत्त्वेभ्यः अधिका तत्त्वाधिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: tattvebhyaḥ adhikā tattvādhikā
samasa.explanation: adhikā 'exceeding, beyond' is the head and the tattvas stand to it in the ablative of comparison: 'beyond the tattvas'.

components.meaning: principle of reality; the categories of existence

names.meaning: She who transcends all cosmic categories
names.significance: In Śaiva and Śākta doctrine the world is built of thirty-six tattvas, from earth up to Śiva; She is beyond them all, even the highest.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is tattva + adhikā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

names.meaning: She who is Reality itself, consisting of the tattvas
names.significance: Having gone beyond the tattvas (906), She is also made of them: every principle of the world is Her. Traditionally tattva is also read as Śiva, the highest principle, so that the name makes Her one with Him. Here tattvamayī is a single name; earlier in the hymn (425–427) Bhāskararāya divides the same letters into tat, tvam and ayī.

meaning_check.note: Capitalization tidied; 'Śiva Himself' is a commentarial reading and moved to the significance.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa with quoted words as first member, inside a karmadhāraya made possessive by -in
samasa.vigraha: तत् त्वम् इति पदयोः अर्थः तत्त्वमर्थः; तत्त्वमर्थः एव स्वरूपम् तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपम्; तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: tat tvam iti padayoḥ arthaḥ tattvamarthaḥ; tattvamarthaḥ eva svarūpam tattvamarthasvarūpam; tattvamarthasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) tat-tvam-artha 'the meaning of the words tat and tvam': the two pronouns are quoted from the mahāvākya, so they keep their own form (not the stems tad, yuṣmad), and artha 'meaning' is the head (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) That meaning is identified with svarūpa 'own nature'. (3) The possessive -in: 'She whose own nature is the meaning of tat and tvam'. The m of tvam simply stands before the a of artha; no sound changes.

components.note: svarūpa 'own form, nature' (sva + rūpa) + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She whose very nature is the meaning of tat and tvam, That and thou
names.significance: The Chāndogya Upaniṣad's tat tvam asi, 'That thou art', identifies the meaning of tat (Brahman) with the meaning of tvam (the inner Self); She is what both words finally denote, and their identity.

meaning_check.note: Wording follows the svarūpiṇī ('whose own nature is').

names.previous_split_issues: The old split cut tattva + 'martha'. The words are tat + tvam + artha ('meaning'); there is no word martha, and the reading form is now hyphenated tattvam-artha.

samasa.vigraha: साम्नाम् गानम् सामगानम्; सामगानम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा सामगानप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: sāmnām gānam sāmagānam; sāmagānam priyam yasyāḥ sā sāmagānapriyā
samasa.explanation: (1) sāma-gāna 'the singing of Sāman chants' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; sāman appears as sāma- with loss of the final n). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom the singing of the Sāmans is dear'.

components.meaning: Sāman chant, the melodies of the Sāma Veda
components.note: appears as sāma- in the compound
priya with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is fond of the chanting of the Sāma Veda
names.significance: The Sāman chants are the Veda set to melody; the Bhagavad Gītā says 'among the Vedas I am the Sāma Veda'. She delights in this music of the Veda.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'sAma veda' respelled.

names.previous_split_issues: sāma was given in its compound form; the stem is sāman.

components.note: soma 'the moon; Soma' + the suffix -ya with vṛddhi, feminine

names.meaning: She who is gentle and benign, cool like the moon
names.significance: Saumya is the opposite of fierce: She is mild and pleasing like the moon (soma), though She can also be fierce (827).

meaning_check.note: Repeated wording tidied into one sentence.

samasa.vigraha: सदा शिवः सदाशिवः; सदाशिवस्य कुटुम्बिनी सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadā śivaḥ sadāśivaḥ; sadāśivasya kuṭumbinī sadāśivakuṭumbinī
samasa.explanation: (1) sadā-śiva 'ever auspicious', the name of the deity Sadāśiva (the indeclinable sadā qualifies śiva). (2) kuṭumbinī 'mistress of the household, wife' is the head, with Sadāśiva in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the consort of Sadāśiva
names.significance: Among the five cosmic functions Sadāśiva presides over grace (anugraha); as His household mistress She is the one who carries out that grace.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'sadAshiva' respelled; 'wife' kept in the sense of kuṭumbinī.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: सव्यम् च अपसव्यम् च सव्यापसव्ये; सव्यापसव्ये मार्गौ सव्यापसव्यमार्गौ; सव्यापसव्यमार्गयोः तिष्ठति इति सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: savyam ca apasavyam ca savyāpasavye; savyāpasavye mārgau savyāpasavyamārgau; savyāpasavyamārgayoḥ tiṣṭhati iti savyāpasavyamārgasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) savya-apasavya 'left and right' (dvandva). (2) They qualify mārga 'path' (karmadhāraya): 'the left and right paths'. (3) stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'She who abides in both paths'.

names.meaning: She who occupies (or can be reached by) both the left and right paths of worship
names.significance: Traditionally the left (vāma) and right (dakṣiṇa) modes of Tantric worship both lead to Her, and She abides in each.
names.previous_split_issues: The old split equated savya with 'right' (dakṣiṇa) and apasavya with 'left'; savya normally means 'left', apasavya 'right'.
names.uncertain: savya is mostly 'left' but is occasionally used for 'right' in ritual contexts; the name covers both paths either way.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाः आपदः सर्वापदः; सर्वापदाम् विनिवारिणी सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāḥ āpadaḥ sarvāpadaḥ; sarvāpadām vinivāriṇī sarvāpadvinivāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-āpad 'all calamities' (karmadhāraya). (2) vinivāriṇī 'one who wards off' is the head, with the calamities in the genitive. The final d of āpad is unchanged before v.

components.note: vi + ni + causative of √vṛ 'to cover, restrain' + -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who removes all dangers
names.significance: Traditionally remembering Her name is itself protection in every calamity.
names.previous_split_issues: sarvāpad was left as one row; it is sarva + āpad, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.vigraha: स्वे तिष्ठति इति स्वस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: sve tiṣṭhati iti svasthā
samasa.explanation: stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with sva 'oneself' as the upapada: 'abiding in Herself'; feminine -ā. As an ordinary adjective svastha also means 'healthy, at ease'.

names.meaning: She who abides in Herself; She who is free from all afflictions
names.significance: Resting in Her own nature, She is never disturbed; the everyday sense 'healthy, at ease' gives the second half of the meaning.

samasa.vigraha: स्वस्य भावः स्वभावः; स्वभावेन मधुरा स्वभावमधुरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: svasya bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ; svabhāvena madhurā svabhāvamadhurā
samasa.explanation: (1) sva-bhāva 'one's own nature' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) madhurā 'sweet' is the head, with svabhāva in the instrumental of respect: 'sweet by nature'.

names.meaning: She who is sweet in Her inherent nature
names.significance: Her sweetness is not put on for the devotee: it is Her very nature, the bliss of consciousness.

components.note: from dhī 'thought, wisdom'; traditionally also analysed dhī + √rā 'to give', 'giver of wisdom'

names.meaning: She who is wise; She who gives wisdom
names.significance: Dhīra also means 'steadfast, composed'. The second half of the meaning rests on a traditional etymology, dhiyaṃ rāti, 'She gives wisdom'.
names.uncertain: The sense 'giver of wisdom' depends on the traditional analysis dhī + √rā; the ordinary meanings are 'wise' and 'steadfast'.

samasa.vigraha: धीरैः समर्चिता धीरसमर्चिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: dhīraiḥ samarcitā dhīrasamarcitā
samasa.explanation: The participle samarcitā 'well worshipped' is the head and the wise are its agents in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by the wise
names.significance: The Kaṭha Upaniṣad calls the dhīra the one who turns the gaze within and sees the Self; such steadfast sages worship Her.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification)
samasa.vigraha: चैतन्यम् एव अर्घ्यम् चैतन्यार्घ्यम्; चैतन्यार्घ्येण समाराध्या चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: caitanyam eva arghyam caitanyārghyam; caitanyārghyeṇa samārādhyā caitanyārghyasamārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) caitanya-arghya 'the arghya that is consciousness' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) The gerundive samārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head, with that offering as its instrument.

components.meaning: arghya, the water of welcome offered to an honored guest or deity

components.note: sam + ā + √rādh + the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who is to be worshipped with consciousness as the arghya offering
names.significance: In inner worship the arghya is not water but consciousness itself, offered back to its source.

meaning_check.note: 'oblation' replaced by arghya, the water of welcome; samārādhyā is 'to be worshipped'.

names.previous_split_issues: caitanyārghya was left as one row; it is caitanya + arghya.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification)
samasa.vigraha: चैतन्यम् एव कुसुमम् चैतन्यकुसुमम्; चैतन्यकुसुमम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: caitanyam eva kusumam caitanyakusumam; caitanyakusumam priyam yasyāḥ sā caitanyakusumapriyā
samasa.explanation: (1) caitanya-kusuma 'the flower that is consciousness' (rūpaka). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom that flower is dear'.

components.note: priya with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is fond of the flower that is consciousness
names.significance: Traditionally inner virtues such as non-violence, self-control and compassion are the 'flowers' of mental worship; the flower of pure consciousness is the dearest to Her.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: tatpuruṣa of an indeclinable with a participle (sup-supā samāsa)
samasa.vigraha: सदा उदिता सदोदिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadā uditā sadoditā
samasa.explanation: The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies the participle uditā 'risen', the head: 'ever risen'.

names.meaning: She who is ever risen, ever shining
names.significance: Unlike the sun She never sets: consciousness is always present, in waking, dream and sleep alike.

meaning_check.note: uditā 'risen' made explicit.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is sadā + uditā, joined by guṇa.

samasa.type: tatpuruṣa of an indeclinable with a participle (sup-supā samāsa)
samasa.vigraha: सदा तुष्टा सदातुष्टा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadā tuṣṭā sadātuṣṭā
samasa.explanation: The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies the participle tuṣṭā 'pleased', the head.

names.meaning: She who is ever pleased
names.significance: Being full in Herself She is always content, and so is easily pleased by Her devotees.
names.previous_split_issues: sadā was glossed 'true/good'; it is the adverb 'always'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तरुणः आदित्यः तरुणादित्यः; तरुणादित्यः इव पाटला तरुणादित्यपाटला
samasa.vigraha_iast: taruṇaḥ ādityaḥ taruṇādityaḥ; taruṇādityaḥ iva pāṭalā taruṇādityapāṭalā
samasa.explanation: (1) taruṇa-āditya 'the young (rising) sun' (karmadhāraya). (2) The standard of comparison is compounded with the word for the shared quality, pāṭalā 'rosy' (upamāna-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.55): 'rosy as the rising sun'.

names.meaning: She who is rosy like the morning sun
names.significance: Her meditation-form is rosy-red like the rising sun, the color of compassion and of the dawn of knowledge.
names.previous_split_issues: taruṇāditya was left as one row; it is taruṇa + āditya.

verse_notes.note: kārya in name 862 is 'effect', paired with kāraṇa 'cause'.
Names 870 and 871 form a pair: to be worshipped by those turned within, very hard to reach for those turned outward.

Names 872–875 each begin with tri-: the three Vedas, the three aims of life, the triads She abides in, and Tripuramālinī of the Śrīcakra. Name 878 is sva + ātma + ārāmā (not svātmā + rāmā); 879 reads sudhāsṛtiḥ (variant sudhāsrutiḥ).
Name 880 fills the whole first half; names 881–883 turn to the Vedic sacrifice.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga after a vowel other than a or ā becomes r before a voiced sound, here y

verse_notes.note: Divide ayonir yoninilayā (894, 895): the r is the visarga of ayoniḥ. The two names are a deliberate paradox: without source, yet the abode of all sources.
Name 905 baindavāsanā: the baindava place is the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra.
Name 907 tattvamayī is a single name here (contrast 425–427 tat / tvam / ayī). Name 908 divides tat-tvam-artha ('the meaning of tat and tvam'), not tattva + martha.
Names 918–919 describe inner worship, with consciousness as the arghya and as the flower.

report.summary: Checked all 61 names of ślokas 161–170 against text.json, with sandhi at every member junction, a layered samāsa analysis and the meanings tested against it. Two old reading forms cut through the words and were re-hyphenated: 878 svātmārāmā (sva + ātma + ārāmā, not svātmā + rāmā) and 908 tattvam-artha-svarūpiṇī (tat + tvam + artha, not tattva + 'martha'). Name 905's meaning was replaced (the baindava place is the bindu of the Śrīcakra, not the spot between the eyebrows); several old glosses were corrected (kārya 'effect', su 'very', sadā 'always', savya 'left'). No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
